title: Jalapeño Poppers
subtitle: Cream-cheese stuffed jalapeños in a crisp breadcrumb crust
excerpt: Jalapeño poppers are halved jalapeño chillies filled with cream cheese and mozzarella, coated in seasoned breadcrumbs, and baked or fried until golden. The filling cools the heat of the chilli and the crisp coating gives the textural contrast that makes them addictive.
sourceNotes: Jalapeño poppers became a standard American bar snack and party food in the 1980s, popularised by chain restaurants. The cream cheese and cheddar filling is the standard American recipe.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking on a tray, then bag. Bake from frozen at 200°C for 25 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch: freeze unbaked poppers and cook as needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Fill and coat the poppers up to a day ahead. Refrigerate until ready to bake.

content.text: Jalapeño poppers are halved chillies stuffed with cream cheese and mozzarella, then coated and baked. The cream cheese cools the chilli heat slightly; the breadcrumb coat goes golden and crisp. These are baked rather than fried, which makes them easier for a larger batch and gives a slightly lighter result.

The seeds and white pith are where most of the chilli's heat sits. Removing them gives a mild to medium result; leaving them in makes the poppers quite hot. Wear disposable gloves when handling a large quantity of raw jalapeños: the capsaicin transfers easily to eyes and skin.

items.prepNote: halved lengthways, seeds and pith removed

content.text: Make the filling and stuff the chillies

Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas mark 6). Mix together {{cream-cheese}}, {{mozzarella}}, {{garlic-powder}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{paprika-smoked}} until combined. Spoon the filling generously into each {{jalapeno-chilli}} half, pressing it in and mounding it slightly.

Set up three dishes: {{plain-flour}} in the first, {{eggs}} in the second, and {{panko}} mixed with {{paprika-smoked}} in the third. Dip each filled chilli half: flour (pressing the filling against the chilli so it stays), then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Arrange on a lined baking tray, filling side up. Drizzle with {{rapeseed-oil}} and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the panko is golden and the cheese is bubbling at the edges.

items.symptom: The filling oozes out during baking
items.cause: Too much filling, or the chilli halves were not deep enough to contain it.
items.fix: Don't overfill: the filling should sit level with the top of the chilli. Press the coating on firmly around the edges to help seal the filling in.

items.symptom: The coating is pale after 20 minutes
items.cause: Not enough oil drizzled over, or oven too low.
items.fix: Make sure each popper gets a thin drizzle of oil before baking. The oil is what makes the panko golden. Alternatively, grill for the last two minutes for colour.

items.symptom: The chillies are still too hot even after cooking
items.cause: Pith and seeds not fully removed.
items.fix: Use a small spoon or melon baller to scrape all the pith out. The inside of the chilli should be smooth and pale green.

items.symptom: The cream cheese filling is lumpy and hard
items.cause: Cream cheese straight from the fridge.
items.fix: Leave the cream cheese at room temperature for 30 minutes before mixing. Cold cream cheese doesn't incorporate smoothly with the other filling ingredients.

content.text: Jalapeño poppers were popularised by American chain restaurants in the 1980s and became a reliable staple of bar menus and party spreads. They sit in the same category as mozzarella sticks: a frying-based snack that uses the contrast between a hot crisp shell and a cool creamy filling. Serve with soured cream and sweet chilli sauce for dipping.
